L0: # List all products
L1: 
L2: Read this page in your terminal: [install the Stripe CLI](https://docs.stripe.com/cli/install) (v1.43.3+) and run `stripe docs`. [Reference](https://docs.stripe.com/cli/docs)
L3: ## Start here: Integrate with Stripe using skills and plugins
L4: 
L5: Stripe provides skills and plugins for agents to build faster and more accurately. See [Agent skills](https://docs.stripe.com/skills.md) for more information.
L6: 
L7: **Quickstart**: Install the Stripe CLI with `npm install -g @stripe/cli` and run `stripe agent setup`.
L8: > Nested parameters, fields, and event types on API reference pages are collapsed by default. Use the provided `?query=<name>` links to show the full definitions. Request the page with an empty `?query=` to expand every entry at once.
L9: 
L10: Returns a list of your products. The products are returned sorted by creation date, with the most recently created products appearing first.
L11: ## Request
L12: 
L13: ```curl
L14: curl -G https://api.stripe.com/v1/products \
L15:   -u "<<YOUR_SECRET_KEY>>" \
L16:   -d limit=3
L17: ```
L18: ### Response
L19: ```json
L20: {
L21:   "object": "list",
L22:   "url": "/v1/products",
L23:   "has_more": false,
L24:   "data": [
L25:     {
L26:       "id": "prod_NWjs8kKbJWmuuc",
L27:       "object": "product",
L28:       "active": true,
L29:       "created": 1678833149,
L30:       "default_price": null,
L31:       "description": null,
L32:       "images": [],
L33:       "marketing_features": [],
L34:       "livemode": false,
L35:       "metadata": {},
L36:       "name": "Gold Plan",
L37:       "package_dimensions": null,
L38:       "shippable": null,
L39:       "statement_descriptor": null,
L40:       "tax_code": null,
L41:       "unit_label": null,
L42:       "updated": 1678833149,
L43:       "url": null
L44:     }
L45:   ]
L46: }
L47: ```
L48: ## Returns
L49: 
L50: A dictionary with a `data` property that contains an array of up to `limit` products, starting after product `starting_after`. Each entry in the array is a separate product object. If no more products are available, the resulting array will be empty.
L51: ## Parameters
L52: 
L53: - `active` (boolean, optional)
L54:   Only return products that are active or inactive (e.g., pass `false` to list all inactive products).
L55: 
L56: - [`created`](https://docs.stripe.com/api/products/list.md?query=created) (object, optional)
L57:   Only return products that were created during the given date interval.
L58: - `ending_before` (string, optional)
L59:   A cursor for use in pagination. `ending_before` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, starting with `obj_bar`, your subsequent call can include `ending_before=obj_bar` in order to fetch the previous page of the list.
L60: - `ids` (array of strings, optional)
L61:   Only return products with the given IDs. Cannot be used with [starting_after](https://docs.stripe.com/api/products/list.md#list_products-starting_after) or [ending_before](https://docs.stripe.com/api/products/list.md#list_products-ending_before).
L62: 
L63: - `limit` (integer, optional)
L64:   A limit on the number of objects to be returned. Limit can range between 1 and 100, and the default is 10.
L65: - `shippable` (boolean, optional)
L66:   Only return products that can be shipped (i.e., physical, not digital products).
L67: 
L68: - `starting_after` (string, optional)
L69:   A cursor for use in pagination. `starting_after` is an object ID that defines your place in the list. For instance, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `obj_foo`, your subsequent call can include `starting_after=obj_foo` in order to fetch the next page of the list.
L70: - `url` (string, optional)
L71:   Only return products with the given url.
